When you state a gradient, write its symbol as the left-hand side of its expression.
"Its gradient is $\tp{(2 x_1,\ -2 x_2)}$" gives the expression a name in words only,
so the reader has no symbol to cite in the steps that follow.
Writing $\gradf{f}(\vx) = \tp{\paren{2 x_1,\ -2 x_2}}$ names the gradient and gives its value together.
Give the gradient its own display when later steps refer to it.

The same holds for any derived quantity that later steps use:

- a Hessian,
- a derivative, and
- a mean [function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/functions.html#def-function).

Write its symbol, an equals sign, and the expression.

::: {#exm-gradient-symbol}

## Writing the gradient with its symbol

> ❌ The gradient of $f(\vx) = x_1^2 - x_2^2$ is $\tp{(2 x_1,\ -2 x_2)}$.
>
> ✅ The gradient of $f(\vx) = x_1^2 - x_2^2$ is
>
> $$
> \gradf{f}(\vx) = \tp{\paren{2 x_1,\ -2 x_2}}.
> $$

The ✅ version supplies $\gradf{f}(\vx)$, which a later line can set equal to $\vzero_{2 \times 1}$.

:::
